titre_page: How to make a Pong game in Yop2D? | Yop2D guide
description: Make a Pong game in Yop2D with no code: a paddle that follows your finger, a robot opponent, bounces, goals and scores with nodes.
h1: How to make a Pong game?
carte: Paddle on your finger, robot opponent, goals and scores.
etapes: A ball, your paddle (Player), a robot (Bot), two walls and two goals, with their exact names and the Scenery behavior.
blocs: In a Pong game, a **ball** bounces between your **paddle** (at the bottom) and the paddle of a **robot** (at the top). When the ball goes behind a paddle, the other player scores. As in the [brick breaker guide](guide:casse-briques), the ball moves thanks to two variables: **vx** (its speed sideways) and **vy** (its speed up or down).
an {{lang:obj_prefix_image}} named **Ball**, in the middle of the screen (for example 60 x 60 px);
an {{lang:obj_prefix_image}} named **Player**, near the bottom (for example 200 x 80 px, around y = 1690);
an {{lang:obj_prefix_image}} named **Bot**, near the top (same size, y = 140);
two {{lang:obj_prefix_texte}} objects named **ScorePlayer** and **ScoreBot**, with the text 0;

This guide is written for a **portrait game of 1080 x 1920**. For the pictures, take the free **Puzzle (brick breaker)** pack (Kenney, CC0) in the **Library**, **Packs to download** tab: **paddleBlu** (your paddle), **paddleRed** (the robot), **ballBlue** (the ball). You can also use your own drawings.
Select each object and write its name in the Inspector, exactly as in the list above. A name with a space or a different letter will not be found by the nodes.
Select **Ball**, touch **⚙ Object behavior** and choose **Scenery**. Do the same for **Player** and **Bot**: only the nodes will move them.

In the **{{lang:panneau_ress_variables}}** section, create two variables of type **{{lang:var_type_chiffre}}**, scope **{{lang:var_scope_locale}}**: **vx** and **vy**, start value **0**. Create two more of type **{{lang:var_type_entier}}**, scope **{{lang:var_scope_locale}}**: **scorePlayer** and **scoreBot**, start value **0**.
**The most common mistake:** a forgotten name or a forgotten behavior. Nothing breaks, but nothing happens. If your game does nothing, check this step first.
The ball bounces on walls that you cannot see: four **{{lang:obj_prefix_zone}}s** around the screen. A zone is invisible during the game, but the ball can touch it.
Add a {{lang:obj_prefix_zone}} named **WallLeft**: X = `-300`, Y = `-400`, width `300`, height `2800`.
Add a {{lang:obj_prefix_zone}} named **WallRight**: X = `1080`, Y = `-400`, width `300`, height `2800`.
Add a {{lang:obj_prefix_zone}} named **GoalBot**: X = `-300`, Y = `-300`, width `1680`, height `300` (above the screen).
Add a {{lang:obj_prefix_zone}} named **GoalPlayer**: X = `-300`, Y = `1920`, width `1680`, height `300` (below the screen).
The walls are thick on purpose: a fast ball cannot pass through them. The two walls send the ball back; the two goals will count the points.
Step 3: the ball starts and moves
Add the event **[[NoeudEventStart]]**, then two **[[modifier_variable]]** nodes in a row: variable **vx**, value `6`, then variable **vy**, value `9`.
Add the event **[[NoeudEventChaqueImage]]**, then **[[pousser]]**: target **Ball**, **Add X** = `vx`, **Add Y** = `vy`. Just write the two names in the fields.

**How does it move?** **[[NoeudEventChaqueImage]]** runs about 60 times per second. Each time, the ball moves by **vx** pixels sideways and **vy** pixels up or down. With 0 and 0, it stops. To change its direction, we only change these two numbers: that is what the bounces will do.
Step 4: my paddle follows my finger
Add the event **[[NoeudEventDoigtAppuye]]**: it repeats while your finger is on the screen.

Add **[[deplacer]]**: target **Player**, **X** = `doigt.x - Player.largeur / 2`, **Y** = `1690`. The finger position is in the list on the left of the settings window; we remove half of the paddle width so that the finger is at its centre.
Add **[[garder_dans_ecran]]**: target **Player**, **Margin** = `0`, so that the paddle cannot leave through the sides.
A bounce is just a new number for **vx** or **vy**. We use **random(a, b)**, which picks a number between a and b: no bounce is the same.
**[[NoeudEventCollisionAB]]** (**Object A** = **WallLeft**, **Object B** = **Ball**) → **[[modifier_variable]]**: **vx** = `random(4, 12)`. A positive number: the ball goes right.
**[[NoeudEventCollisionAB]]** (**WallRight**, **Ball**) → **[[modifier_variable]]**: **vx** = `-random(4, 12)`. The minus sign makes it negative: the ball goes left.

**Why this calculation for the paddle?** It compares the position of the ball with the position of the paddle: in the centre, the ball goes straight; near an edge, it goes sideways. The `-7` compensates for the paddle being wider than the ball (so the centre gives 0).
Step 6: the robot chases the ball
The robot is not clever: on every frame, it moves a little towards the ball.
Add the event **[[NoeudEventChaqueImage]]**, then **[[modifier_propriete]]**: target **Bot**, **Property** = `x`, **Value** = `Bot.x * 0.94 + Ball.x * 0.06 - 6`.

**How does it work?** The robot keeps 94 % of its own place and takes 6 % of the place of the ball (the `- 6` centres it on the ball). With `0.06`, it is slow enough to be beaten. Try `0.03` and `0.97` (very easy) or `0.15` and `0.85` (very hard): the two numbers must add up to 1, and the `- 6` becomes `- 3` or `- 15`.
**Careful:** do not write a position in "speed X". A speed is a small number, a position is a big one: the robot would not move.

To serve again, add in a row: **[[modifier_variable]]** **vx** = `0`, **[[modifier_variable]]** **vy** = `0`, **[[deplacer]]** **Ball** to X = `510`, Y = `930`, **[[attendre]]** 1 second, then **[[modifier_variable]]** **vx** = `6` and **[[modifier_variable]]** **vy** = `9`.
Link the end of the two goals to the **first node** of this serve: an input can receive several wires.
**The `=` in front of the text** tells Yop2D to calculate the value instead of writing it as it is (see the guide [Collecting coins and counting points](guide:pieces-score)).
**Win at 5 points:** after each goal, add a **[[condition]]** `=scorePlayer >= 5`, then a **[[toast]]** and **[[recommencer_scene]]** (see the guide [Lives and Game Over](guide:vie-game-over)).
**Your own look:** change the pictures and the background; the names stay the same.
**The game does nothing?** Go back to step 1: a name or a behavior is missing. **The robot does not move?** Check that its behavior is **Scenery** and that the formula is in **Value**.
